Roofing in Grapevine, Texas

Grapevine is the oldest settlement in Tarrant County, with historic districts downtown, Grapevine Lake on its north side and a firm rule against shingles laid over shingles. One free number connects you with a local roofer.

Call (469) 649-7066 Grapevine's re-roof rules
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Grapevine

Tarrant County's oldest town, on the edge of a big lake

Roofing in Grapevine, TX covers more history than most suburbs can claim. Settlers founded Grape Vine Prairie in 1844, making it the oldest settlement in Tarrant County, and the 1888 arrival of the Cotton Belt rail line turned it into a farm trade center.

The city incorporated in 1907. Then, in 1952, the Army Corps of Engineers finished Grapevine Lake, built under the River and Harbors Act of 1945 to hold back Trinity River floods. Today the lake wraps the city's north side, DFW Airport sits to the south, and Grapevine's limits reach into three counties: Tarrant, Dallas and Denton.

That mix produces three different kinds of roof call: older homes near the historic downtown, decades of suburban houses across the rest of the city, and commercial roofs around the hotels, shops and offices. DFW Expert Roofers handles none of them itself. It is a free phone line that answers and connects you with an independent, locally owned roofer working in Grapevine.

December 13, 2022: two tornadoes in one morning

The storm Grapevine residents remember best came before dawn in mid-December, during a North Texas outbreak in which the National Weather Service confirmed 16 tornadoes.

  1. The first track. NWS surveyors rated it EF-1 with winds near 110 mph. It ran from around the Sam's Club area to southwest of the Gaylord Texan and lifted at the lakeshore.
  2. The second track. A short EF-1, near 100 mph, touched down at Grapevine Mills, damaging the mall and nearby stores.
  3. Homes hit. Houses along Lucas Drive near Northwest Highway had roof and tree damage, and the city counted more than 40 structures affected.
  4. The toll. Mayor William D. Tate reported five minor injuries and no deaths.

Wind damage is not always obvious. Shingles can be lifted and creased without falling off, which breaks their seal and lets the next rain in. After a storm, look from the yard for shingles out of line or missing, and call your insurer before permanent repairs.

What Grapevine expects from a re-roof

The City of Grapevine spells out its residential re-roofing rules on a single sheet from Building Services, at 200 S. Main Street. A homeowner who knows them can spot a roofer who does not.

A permit comes first

Grapevine will not let a re-roof start without one. The work follows the 2021 International Residential Code, Section R908 for re-roofing.

No shingles over shingles

Asphalt shingles may not be installed over an existing roof covering. Every asphalt re-roof here is a tear-off, which exposes the decking for a look.

Vents done right

The sheet calls for roof vents to be properly connected and flashed as part of the permit. Ask the roofer how it handles each pipe and vent.

Registered roofers

Grapevine registers roofing contractors as general contractors, and registration is required before permitted work. Owner-occupants are the exemption.

Inspections are on you too

The city puts the duty to get inspections on the permit applicant and the property owner. If inspections are not passed, the permit expires.

Who to call

Inspections are requested at 817-410-3010. Permit and registration questions go to Building Services at 817-410-3165.

Roofs in Grapevine's historic districts

Grapevine protects its old downtown and several historic districts. For a house in one of them, or a designated landmark, a Certificate of Appropriateness must be approved before exterior alterations. City staff can approve simple, routine changes within a few days of the application; bigger projects go before the Historic Preservation Commission, which meets once a month.

The district design guidelines include a roof section. They favor repairing original features and replacing them only when they are past repair, with new material that matches the old in design and appearance. A Certificate of Appropriateness is not a building permit, so the roofer still pulls the regular re-roof permit. Before choosing shingles for a historic house, call the preservation office at 817-410-3197. Staff help costs nothing.

Planning a roof on an older Grapevine house, or dealing with wind damage after a storm? Call and describe it. The roofer you reach sees the house in person, can talk through the city steps, and gives you its price in writing.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Questions for a roofer in Grapevine

  • Are you registered with the City of Grapevine, and will you pull the re-roof permit before tear-off?
  • Does your price include removing every existing layer, as the city requires?
  • How will you connect and flash each roof vent?
  • If my house is in a historic district, will you help with the Certificate of Appropriateness material samples?
  • Who requests the inspections, and how will I know they passed?
  • Will your insurer send me your liability certificate, and will the shingle maker's warranty be registered under my name?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Grapevine roof questions

Do you need a permit for roof repair in Grapevine TX?

A full re-roof does. Grapevine puts re-roofing on its permit list alongside windows and siding, and its residential re-roofing sheet covers what the inspector expects. Smaller repairs can be a gray area, so ask Building Services at 817-410-3165 whether your job needs one. Either way, the roofer must be registered with the city before doing permitted work. A typical repair visit is described on the roof repair page.

Can a roofer put new shingles over my old roof in Grapevine?

Not with asphalt shingles. Grapevine's re-roofing requirements say asphalt shingles may not be installed over existing roof coverings, so the old roof comes off first. That lets the roofer and inspector see the decking. If a quote is noticeably cheaper than the rest, ask whether it includes a full tear-off.

My Grapevine home is in a historic district. What do I need for a new roof?

Plan on a Certificate of Appropriateness before exterior work, and a building permit as well, since the city says one does not replace the other. Routine changes can be approved by staff within a few days; larger ones go to the Historic Preservation Commission, which meets monthly. The design guidelines favor repairing original roofing and matching it when it must be replaced. Call the preservation office at 817-410-3197 first.

What happens when I call about a Grapevine roof?

An automated assistant for DFW Expert Roofers answers at any hour. The line is free and is not a roofing company. It notes the problem and your part of town, then hands you over to a locally owned roofer, independent of the line, that works in Grapevine. That roofer handles the inspection, estimate, permit and work, and you pay it directly. Roofers may pay the line for referrals. How the line works.
